1766.title: Replacing a local plugin source destroys its settings silently: remove is the only supported path and it deletes plugin_settings
1766.rootCauseOneLine: Registration refuses a same-id path: install from a different directory (plugin-registration.ts assertInstallRegistrationAvailable) and `update` is a no-op for path rows, so the only route is remove+install; PluginService.remove() unconditionally deletes plugin_settings, plugin schedules and the secrets dir (plugin-service.ts ~L1681-1694) with no log/warning, and CLI help + the local-plugin UI dialog describe remove as non-destructive.
1766.proposedFix: Allow an in-place path->path replace for the same plugin id in apps/server/src/services/plugins/plugin-registration.ts (relax assertInstallRegistrationAvailable when existing.sourceKind==="path" && intent.kind==="path" && provenance is direct; dispose old instance, upsert row with new sourcePath/rootDir, forgetMutableRoot(old), loadOne) -- settings/secrets/schedules are keyed by plugin id only so they survive; optionally gate behind `bb plugin install --replace` / POST /plugins {replace:true}. Independently make remove honest and loud: update CLI description (apps/cli/src/commands/plugin.ts:1846), guide text (bb-guide-plugins.md:221) and the local-plugin ConfirmDeleteDialog copy in apps/app/src/views/ToolsView.tsx:366 to say settings/secrets/schedules are deleted, and add a logger.info in remove(). Optionally keep deleting only the secrets dir on remove and retain plugin_settings/schedules. No host-daemon wire change, no protocol version bump.
1766.caveats: Bundle line numbers cited in the issue (bb 0.38 start-server.js) were not checked against the release bundle; the TS source at HEAD matches the quoted code and the behaviour dates to the original plugin-system commit 66ddc6018, so it is present in HEAD (not fixed). Repro test file was left uncommitted in the worktree at apps/server/test/services/plugins/issue-1766-local-replace-loses-settings.test.ts. Dev instance stopped.

1747.title: npx install pins bb to one minor line, so the update button silently does nothing
1747.rootCauseOneLine: The claimed npx "^0.35.1 hard pin" does not exist (npx re-resolves @latest on every run — verified with the reporter's exact cache entry, 0.35.1 -> 0.38.0); the web surface simply has no self-update (Copy-command only), and re-running `npx bb-app@latest` while the old bb is still running makes the launcher falsely print "bb is ready" (waitForHealth accepts the old server's /health) while its children EADDRINUSE-crash-loop and the URL keeps serving 0.35.1 — same root cause as #1558.

prReviews.topFinding: Docs-only PR whose central claim (npx bb-app@latest pins to ^0.35.1 and can never update) is false: libnpmexec (npm 7..11.17) re-resolves the latest tag via preferOnline and compares resolved tarballs, and an empirical run against the reporter's exact cache entry upgraded 0.35.1 -> 0.38.0. It also claims 'restarting is a real update' for npm install --prefix (only re-running npm install updates), recommends installing into ~/.bb (bb's data dir), leaves the app's own upgradeCommand contradicting the README, and omits the one instruction that matters (stop the running bb first).

1747.proposedFix: (1) packages/bb-app/src/launcher.ts: make readiness prove the spawned child answered — pass a per-launch nonce to the server/daemon children (env), echo it from GET /health (apps/server/src/server.ts) and the daemon status probe, and require a match in waitForHealth/waitForHostDaemonStatus; treat claimBbAppRuntimeFile()===false with a live pid as a hard error ("bb <ver> already runs (pid N); run `npx bb-app stop` then re-run"), and cap immediate crash-restart loops. (2) UI/docs: web Updates row + README/packages/bb-app README should say "stop the running bb (Ctrl+C or npx bb-app stop), then run npx bb-app@latest" — do NOT claim npx cannot update. (3) Optional: log currentVersion vs registry latest at server startup for visibility.
1747.caveats: Could not observe the reporter's machine; the false-ready path is the most plausible explanation for their experience but not proven to be what they did. An npmrc with prefer-offline=true (or offline=true) WOULD pin npx to the cached packument (verified: cache hit, no revalidation) — worth asking the reporter for `npm config get prefer-offline offline` and `npm -v`. Tests used isolated npm cache and data dir with real registry downloads of bb-app 0.35.1/0.38.0; the launcher false-ready is verified with the packaged 0.38.0 launcher, and the same waitForHealth code exists unchanged at base commit 16ceb3a54. No unit test was written for the launcher bug because waitForHealth/startFullStackServerProcess are not exported; the shell repro exercises the exact code path.

1746.title: Plugin background services can kill the server: supervisor only sees the promise chain
1746.rootCauseOneLine: Plugins run in-process and background services are supervised only via the start() promise (plugin-runtime.ts runService), while the server registers only an observe-only uncaughtExceptionMonitor (process-utils installSafeProcessDiagnostics) and no unhandledRejection handler, so any out-of-band plugin error (unlistened EventEmitter 'error', timer throw, detached rejection) exits the server, which restarts, reloads the plugin, and crash-loops with no plugin attribution in the dump.
1746.proposedFix: (1) Attribution: wrap every plugin entry point (factory, runService, schedule ticks, handlers) in an AsyncLocalStorage store {pluginId, surface} owned by plugin-runtime, and let installSafeProcessDiagnostics accept an attribution() hook merged into the crash report; also add an unhandledRejection handler that writes a report (verified ALS store is visible in uncaughtExceptionMonitor/unhandledRejection for emitter error, timer throw, and detached rejection on Node 24). (2) Containment: add an uncaughtException handler that, only when the store attributes the throw to a plugin, routes it into onServiceSettled's existing backoff, counts crashes per plugin, and auto-disables after N crashes with a visible status; unattributed throws keep today's exit. (3) Crash-loop breaker: persist a per-plugin last-load marker so a plugin whose load precedes repeated fast server deaths starts disabled. Optional larger step: worker_threads per plugin.
1746.caveats: Reporter's production counts (1321 dumps, 1613 replaced sessions) are unverifiable but consistent with the mechanism. In my repro the daemon reconnected to the same session across several fast restarts, so replaced-session count (4) was lower than crash count (14). I did not run a live agent thread during the crash loop, so the "Thread interrupted because the host daemon disconnected" message was verified by code path (session-owner-side-effects.ts -> thread-lifecycle.ts), not observed. In my repro the dump stack happens to include the plugin path because the throwing timer lives in the plugin file; with imapflow the frame is in node_modules so no plugin name appears, as the issue states. Issue line numbers (runService L427, process-utils L257/L271) are stale vs main (L557, L327/L321) but the code is unchanged in substance. Type/Priority/Effort pills are my classification; the issue has no project fields set.

1717.title: `auto` permission mode does not actually restrict the workspace with current codex/claude CLIs
1717.rootCauseOneLine: bb maps its `auto` preset onto Claude Code's native `auto` (classifier) mode, which approves tool calls without ever invoking the SDK canUseTool callback where all of bb's workspace policy lives — and the bwrap sandbox backstop is silently disabled (failIfUnavailable:false, socat missing) and never covered Write/Edit anyway; on Codex the workspace-write sandbox holds but the guardian auto-reviewer approves the escalation and bb drops the review events as noise, so the escape is invisible (approvalStatus null).
1717.proposedFix: Claude Code: stop relying on canUseTool for the workspace boundary in auto mode — either run the SDK in acceptEdits and implement the "automatic review" (in-workspace allow / out-of-workspace or unsandboxed-retry deny) in the bridge's canUseTool, or keep the classifier but add a PreToolUse hook that hard-denies out-of-workspace Write/Edit paths and dangerouslyDisableSandbox (verify hooks are honoured in auto mode first); when permissionScope is workspace and the sandbox is unavailable, fail closed or emit a visible event instead of silent degradation; read the effective permissionMode from the SDK init message and surface/handle the silent auto→default downgrade for ineligible models. Codex: translate item/autoApprovalReview/* and guardianWarning into a recorded approvalStatus (approved/denied automatically) plus a normalized event instead of noise/provider-unhandled. Product: either honour "same workspace sandbox" (no out-of-workspace completion without a bb-visible decision) or fix the picker copy/runbook, and consider defaulting new threads to accept-edits until then; add a live probe (out-of-workspace write under $HOME per provider/mode) to the QA suite.
1717.caveats: Revision: all four repro scripts were made portable (BB_REPO + scripts/bb-dev-app env, any cwd, inherited BB_SERVER_URL deliberately ignored) and the entire repro was re-executed on a fresh worktree/instance (wf_debcf606-e4a-32, :22884); §4 outputs are now verbatim re-run outputs and both SDK-probe transcripts are unabridged. Note: an intermediate draft of the scripts that trusted the inherited BB_SERVER_URL registered the qa-1717 project on the user's real :38886 instance; it was deleted immediately (verified absent) and no threads were spawned there. In this re-run Codex answered BLOCKED after a failed byte-count self-check even though the out-of-workspace file was written (8 bytes, ESCAPED\n) — the report now instructs readers to judge by the filesystem; tool choice (fileChange vs commandExecution) is nondeterministic. Unchanged caveats: the issue's "9 residual PART A live-test failures" remain unverifiable; the Claude bwrap sandbox on this host is disabled (socat missing) so the sandbox-active + unsandboxed-retry path was not tested; Codex guardian approval is arguably by design (bb-side defect there is visibility). Screenshots are from the original run (states identical in re-run). Dev instance stopped; worktree left clean at base commit.

1706.title: queued thread messages can silently vanish: reported accepted, never delivered, no longer queued
1706.rootCauseOneLine: No permanent-drop path found (accept and drain are transactional); the "accepted, not in log, not in queue" state arises because `bb thread queue list` hides claimed rows (in-flight drain, or an orphaned claim after a server restart mid-drain, which is only released by the 5-minute stale-claim sweep — now exercised for real in exp. H), `bb thread tell`/send returns no receipt to distinguish started vs queued, and `bb thread log` is a window (last 20 segments; --json = oldest 100 events).
1706.proposedFix: 1) Make POST /threads/:id/messages return a receipt ({outcome:"started"|"queued", requestId?, queuedMessageId?}) and have `bb thread tell` print/expose it; 2) make listQueuedThreadMessages / `bb thread queue list` include claimed rows with a state field ("queued"|"sending") instead of hiding them (treat "sending" rows as read-only in the app reorder/edit code), and consider releasing orphaned claims at server startup instead of waiting 5 minutes; 3) make `bb thread log --format json` return newest events (or add --all) and print timeline page metadata so agents know they saw a window; 4) optionally surface drain failures/deferrals as a system row on the target thread.
1706.caveats: Revision addressed all verifier findings: repro scripts are now parameterized (BB_REPO env, thread id argument, bb.db discovered via `scripts/bb-dev-app status`) and were re-run on a fresh instance (worktree wf_debcf606-e4a-38, server :22889) with real output pasted; permalinks corrected against 16ceb3a54 (#L513-L519, #L125, #L601-L607, start-server.ts#L255-L258); the "claim persists after server restart" statement is now exercised for real (exp. H: real drain claim caught 10 ms after write, server kill -9, supervisor restart, row hidden/claimed until sweep delivered it 5m06s later); plain-language glossary added to the TL;DR; Verification subsection added. Still could not reproduce a permanent message loss on main with codex; the reporter's fleet version/provider are unknown; the unit test documents current behavior (passes on main) rather than failing. Note for readers: running `scripts/bb-dev-app current` a second time restarts the instance (my first re-run did this from inside the script and the target thread ended in error) — the scripts use `status`. Control experiments A/B/C were parameterized but not re-run (outputs are from the original run). No screenshots (CLI-only issue).

1660.title: bb host process grew to 77GB RSS and froze the machine; orphaned dev processes in deleted managed worktrees compound the leak
1660.rootCauseOneLine: Environment teardown (RuntimeManager.destroyEnvironment -> runtime.shutdown() on the direct bridge child, then removeWorktree rm -rf) never enumerates or signals processes rooted in the worktree; agent-started background processes survive with a (deleted) cwd — and, since Claude Code runs its Bash tool in a new session (detached:true), they are not even in the bridge's process group, so only a cwd scan can find them. The 77GB RSS growth itself is unreproduced (no RSS ceiling/telemetry; daemon event-sink queue deliberately unbounded).
1660.proposedFix: (1, covers the reproduced case) In RuntimeManager.destroyEnvironment, before workspace.destroy(), scan for processes whose cwd is inside the worktree (/proc/*/cwd on Linux, lsof -d cwd / proc_pidinfo on macOS), SIGTERM->SIGKILL them, return the reaped list in the environment.destroy result (bump HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION) and record a thread event; also run the same scan periodically for processes with a (deleted) cwd under the managed worktrees root. (2, defence in depth, does NOT reach the reproduced orphan because Claude Code's Bash tool already setsid's) Spawn bridges/terminal shells detached as group leaders and kill(-pid) on shutdown, reusing killSetupScriptProcess from packages/host-workspace/src/provisioning.ts. (3) host.resources RPC (defaultReadResourceUsage + child RSS + deleted-cwd count) surfaced via `bb status --resources`; make the health monitor warn on RSS on all platforms. (4) Explicit --max-old-space-size from the launcher and a byte cap on the daemon event-sink queue.
1660.caveats: Revision addressed all three verifier findings with fresh evidence: re-ran the live repro (thr_g3xmvwtd84 / env_ig2nscwucq) capturing pgid/sid — orphan sleep pgid 1593823/sid 1593772 vs bridge+claude pgid/sid 1581708 — plus a strings dump of the claude 2.1.234 binary showing the Bash tool spawns with detached:!0; reordered the fix list so the cwd scan is primary and the group-kill is explicitly scoped. Dropped the #1584 attribution (git blame: runtime.shutdown() before workspace.destroy() dates from b04593eb87, 2026-03-24; bridge/claude stayed alive during the whole retiring window and died only at destroy); the #1769 12h46m survival is now marked unexplained. Repro steps now say `bb` = `pnpm bb:dev`, show `pnpm bb:dev machine list` for the host id, and were re-recorded from the revision run; find-worktree-procs.sh now prints pgid/sid. Unit test re-run still fails at line 101. The 77GB RSS growth remains unreproduced (needs a day of macOS load; report gives no PID/heap data). Ran on Linux; the /proc scanner is Linux-only. Dev instance stopped.

1650.title: Messages to a thread blocked on AskUserQuestion are dropped, and only the sender is told
1650.rootCauseOneLine: Two guards keyed on hasPendingThreadInteraction drop inbound traffic to a blocked thread with no persistence: the /send route (all bb thread tell modes, incl. queue-if-active per PR #112) throws 409 before anything is stored, and queueParentSystemMessage silently returns false for child-completed/failed notices with no log or retry.

prReviews.topFinding: Right design (queues sends, persists deferred parent notices) and my repro test passes on it, but it is 26 commits behind main and collides with main's migration idx 99 (0099_flawless_maximus vs 0099_deferred_parent_system_messages) plus 8 other conflicts (plugin SDK version 0.4.7 vs main 0.4.8, snapshot/journal, server.ts, SKILL.md); also flushDeferredParentSystemMessages deletes the row before delivery, so a flush that fails (parent 'stopping' when its interaction is interrupted, host disconnected) permanently loses the notice despite the advertised sweep — demonstrated by probe (b).

Targets #1655, not this issue (only rewrites the 409 text and adds CLI visibility/wait --until-input); tests pass, but it is stale (plugin SDK bump 0.4.7 conflicts with main's 0.4.8, bundled d.ts/templates conflicts) and edits the same 409 assertions/guide/SDK files as #1699, so it needs a rebase and will conflict with whichever lands first.

1650.proposedFix: Server: (1) in the /send route, when the target has a pending interaction and mode != start, persist via createQueuedMessageForThread and return 200 {ok, delivery:"queued", queuedReason:"awaiting_user_interaction"} instead of calling ensureThreadIsNotAwaitingUserInteraction (delete the #112 guard call at routes/threads/actions.ts:326 and flip its regression test); keep 409 only for mode start. (2) In queueParentSystemMessage, never return false silently for a blocked parent: persist the notice durably, log at info, flush on a PendingInteractionLifecycle settle hook and from the periodic sweep, and delete the row only after a successful send (claim/release, not delete-then-send). (3) Guard sendNextQueuedMessageIfPresent against pending interactions and re-kick the queue when an interaction settles on an idle thread. (4) Surface delivery/queuedReason in the SDK and bb thread tell, and document in guide + bb-cli skill; consider flushing queued tells on settle as steers so worker reports do not wait for the whole turn. No HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed (no daemon wire change).
1650.caveats: The reporter's 'bus room', 'wake failures' and watchdog are external tooling; only bb's 409 and bb's own parent-notification drop were verified. Live repro used claude-code (haiku) with native AskUserQuestion; codex/pi plugin AskUserQuestion path not exercised live but goes through the same pending-interaction guards. Screenshots are of the web app timeline (before/after), the CLI evidence is text. First run of the repro script accidentally hit the user's real bb (:38886) via inherited BB_SERVER_URL; only reads and a failed tell to a nonexistent thread id occurred there. Unit test first needed seedThreadRuntimeState to be a faithful fixture (500 'no stored execution model' otherwise); with it, it fails on main (409) and passes on PR #1699. Both PRs share base ba426545; PR #1699 description ('defer in server memory') is stale relative to its code (persists to a new table).

1647.title: Deleting a worktree environment leaves its processes running
1647.rootCauseOneLine: RuntimeManager.destroyEnvironment only SIGTERM/SIGKILLs the direct provider bridge pid and SIGHUPs the terminal shell pid (spawned in the daemon's own process group, no group signal, no cwd sweep) before `git worktree remove --force`, so anything those children detached (nohup dev servers, background jobs, MCP servers after a force-kill, or processes from a pre-restart daemon) survives with a deleted cwd and is never reaped.

prReviews.verdict: REQUEST CHANGES (minor) — fixes root cause, tests pass, live retest reaps all leaked processes; wants leader-first SIGTERM ordering and explicit call-out that the cwd sweep kills processes bb never started
prReviews.topFinding: killProcessesWithCwdUnder is ownership-agnostic: it SIGTERM/SIGKILLs any user process whose cwd is inside the workspace (demonstrated with a non-bb `setsid sleep` rooted in the worktree, pid 1641293 reaped), i.e. a user's own shell/editor terminal in the worktree dies on environment delete — acceptable but undocumented; secondary: group-SIGTERM as the first signal races the bridge's graceful onSigterm path (send to leader first, group on escalation), and PR description is stale about ACP agents (reverted in commit 2).

1647.proposedFix: Two daemon-side layers, no protocol bump: (1) spawn provider CLIs / setup scripts / command terminals as POSIX process-group leaders (detached:true) and signal the group on shutdown, with escalation keyed on 'any group member alive' — but SIGTERM the leader first so the bridge's graceful shutdown still drives the CLI down, group-signal only at the SIGKILL escalation; (2) before workspace.destroy() for a managed workspace, list processes whose cwd is at/under the workspace (Linux /proc/*/cwd, macOS lsof -d cwd), SIGTERM, short grace, rescan, SIGKILL, and log the reaped pids; optionally add a one-time daemon-start sweep for '(deleted)' cwds under the worktrees root to clean up already-leaked machines. PR #1696 implements essentially this.
1647.caveats: The '12h-old claude process' from #1769 was not reproduced: in my idle and mid-turn runs the claude-code bridge handled SIGTERM gracefully and took claude with it; leaking the CLI itself needs the 5s SIGKILL fallback or a daemon restart before destroy (both real code paths, not provoked live). All reproduction is on Linux; macOS uses the same daemon code path but its lsof-based sweep in the PR was not exercised here. Issue has no Priority/Effort project fields; pills in the report are proposals. Some earlier artifacts from a prior interrupted run existed in the repro dir and were removed; the unit repro test file (originally left by that run) was re-executed by me on both main (fails) and PR head (passes).

1646.title: Codex thread shows `idle` (no spinner) while actively running commands
1646.rootCauseOneLine: Server (and daemon) derive thread activity solely from root turn/started + turn/completed; root work (item/started etc.) that a provider streams afterwards under an already-started turn id passes the stored-turn/started guard and is persisted, but never flips the thread back to active — and since #1640 the daemon grammar silently drops the provider's second turn/completed for that turn.

prReviews.topFinding: Relies on a second turn/completed for the same turn to settle the reactivated thread, but on current main (since #1640) the daemon's ThreadEventGrammar drops that duplicate completion (turn/settles-once) silently — verified live on pr-1697 merged onto 16ceb3a54: thread reactivates (spinner returns) then stays `active` indefinitely (bb thread wait times out) until a manual stop. Also based on ba4265453 with a merge conflict against main (deleted RuntimeTurnReplayFilter tests), no guard against stale items on old turns reactivating, and misstates the pre-PR stop behaviour (release/kill, not no-op).

1646.proposedFix: Server: on a root item/started for a completed turn (idle thread, no stop since that turn's request, no newer root turn started) apply run.started, and settle back to idle when the reopened work itself settles (last open root item on that turn completes) rather than depending on a duplicate turn/completed. Daemon: let ThreadEventGrammar accept a re-completion of a turn that root work reopened (move it back to startedTurnIds) and log grammar drops at warn level instead of discarding onStderr; reopen RuntimeTurnState's active turn on such work so thread/stop sends turn/interrupt instead of releasing/killing the session. Add server-warn telemetry for 'root work on completed turn' so the Codex-side trigger becomes diagnosable.
1646.caveats: The provider-side trigger (why Codex emits root work under a turn id it already completed) is unverified: real Codex 0.147.0 on a trivial prompt showed no such continuation, and Codex main source runs Stop hooks and mid-turn compaction before TurnComplete while mailbox continuations open new turn ids; reporter's Codex version/hooks and raw event log would settle it. Bug reproduced end to end using a scripted codex app-server behind the real bridge/daemon/server (PATH shim + login-shell wrapper), not with real Codex traffic. An alternative reading of the report (mislabelled sub-agent turn completion flipping the parent idle) is consistent with the evidence and would NOT be fixed by #1697. Unread-dot behaviour not exercised.

1621.title: Non-Latin-1 chars (em dash) in interaction/secret-request text crash server response serialization; client sees only 'fetch failed'
1621.rootCauseOneLine: Two unrelated things: (a) the secrets/plugin-CLI/interaction path never puts text into headers (em-dash requests succeed end to end); the user-visible 'hangs then fetch failed' is the CLI's single bare fetch() to POST /api/v1/plugins/secrets/cli hitting undici's default 300 s headersTimeout while the human fills the form, which aborts the pending interaction; (b) the logged ByteString TypeError is a real bug in the bundled tasks plugin: its attachment download route puts the raw attachment file name into Content-Disposition filename="..." (sanitizeFileName keeps non-Latin-1 chars), and @hono/node-server's lazily-validated Response makes Hono log it (levels at or outside compress)+1 times per request (4 on 0.37.0, 5 on main) while the client gets a JSON 500 / broken .
1621.proposedFix: (1) plugins/tasks/attachments/index.ts download route: follow RFC 6266 -- filename="<ASCII fallback: fileName.replace(/[^\x20-\x7e]/g,'-') with quotes/backslashes stripped>"; filename*=UTF-8''<encoded> (or drop filename= and keep only filename*); the failing unit test plugins/tasks/attachments/issue-1621-non-latin1-filename.test.ts encodes the expected header. (2) Harden packages/plugin-sdk/src/internal/host-policy.ts adoptHttpRouteResponse to always rebuild new Response(body, {status, statusText, headers: new Headers(value.headers)}) so an invalid header value throws once at the plugin invoke boundary and becomes one structured 500 attributed to the plugin instead of a late 'set res' crash logged N times; optionally map ByteString TypeErrors in errorToResponse to 'invalid characters in a response header'. (3) Make POST /api/v1/plugins/:id/cli immune to idle timeouts: flush headers immediately and stream NDJSON heartbeats every ~20-30 s while the plugin command runs, then a final result line; update runPluginCliCommand in apps/cli/src/plugin-cli-proxy.ts to consume the stream (server<->CLI only, no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump; verify heartbeats flush through the connect tunnel). Cheaper alternative: undici Agent({headersTimeout:0, bodyTimeout:0}) as dispatcher for that call. (4) In runPluginCliCommand print err.cause?.code/message (e.g. UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT) instead of the bare 'fetch failed'. Do not encode secrets text into headers -- the secrets path never puts it there.
1621.caveats: The tasks-attachment source of the reporter's 12 log lines is inferred from the identical message/stack, the per-request count rule (4 on 0.37.0) and the index arithmetic (35/43/46 = 'inline; filename="' or 'attachment; filename="' prefix + dash offset); the reporter did not include the header value, so which route/files produced their burst is not proven, only shown to be a bundled bb entry point that reproduces it exactly. The 300 s headersTimeout explanation of 'fetch failed' is verified empirically (301 s, UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT) but the reporter's exact hold duration is unknown. The §4.2 UI screenshots and cancel/describe logs are retained from the first-pass instance (ports 22666, thread thr_m5apn4t6y5); §4.1, §4.3, §4.4, §4.5 and both unit tests were run fresh in this revision on the :22837 instance, which was stopped with pnpm dev:stop. The tasks-plugin unit test uses the fake plugin host, where the global Response validates eagerly, so it fails with a 500 from the harness rather than the deferred N+1 log lines; the live run and the apps/server mechanism test cover the deferred behaviour.

1612.title: Recursive tool schemas (z.json()) break Grok 4.6: every turn fails with a generic provider error
1612.rootCauseOneLine: Schema shape verified (zod 4 z.json() emits a self-referential #/$defs/__schema0 for bb_workflow_run.args / bb_workflow_result.value) but Grok 4.6 accepts it today with the reporter's exact cursor-agent build (raw ACP flat+recursive, and inside bb with the workflows plugin explicitly enabled); separately, main since #1640 builds the ACP dynamic-tool MCP server command from process.argv[1] (now the provider-bridge bootstrap), which rejects --mcp-stdio and exits 1, so ACP agents never receive any bb dynamic tool — still present on origin/main after #1613 merged.

prReviews.verdict: MERGED (c25298f69, 2026-08-18T05:37Z) — post-merge findings; would have been REQUEST CHANGES
prReviews.topFinding: Part (a) (z.unknown() for the two workflow tools) is fine as merged; part (b) adds a global registration-time rejection of any recursive $ref (plugin-api.ts:1029 / plugin-service.ts:777) that fails whole plugins and silently drops a plugin's entire configure() output for all providers, to satisfy a Grok 4.6 rejection that no longer reproduces — recommend softening to flatten-with-warning as a follow-up; also cannot be validated end-to-end against Cursor on main because the ACP bridge's MCP server never starts (#1640 regression, still on origin/main).

One-line primaryModels change to packages/agent-runtime/src/acp/profiles.ts, a file #1640 removed; CONFLICTING on main (policy now in packages/agent-runtime/src/acp-launch-specs.ts:30-38); unrelated to the schema bug.
All touched files moved to plugins/provider-acp by #1640 and HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 130 on main (PR bumps 123->124); CONFLICTING/DIRTY, needs full rebase; explicitly does not address #1612.

1529.title: Persistent shell session wedges silently when its stored cwd is deleted (git worktree remove); all subsequent spawns return no exit status
1529.rootCauseOneLine: The "persistent shell" is Cursor's Shell tool (bb provider acp-cursor): its executor re-spawns each command with cwd = the cwd persisted from the last state dump, Node's spawn fails with ENOENT once that directory is deleted, the error is thrown instead of yielding an exit event (Cursor backend: "returned no exit status"), and the stored cwd is only repaired after a successful run, so it stays wedged until a working_directory override; bb additionally fabricates exitCode 0 for these (and for genuinely non-zero) Cursor calls in plugins/provider-acp/src/event-translation.ts because it derives exit codes from ACP status alone.
1529.proposedFix: Upstream (Cursor CLI, file with repro): in BashState/ZshState.execute stat the resolved cwd before spawn; if missing fall back to the request/session working directory (or nearest existing ancestor), reset this.cwd, prepend a warning line, and convert spawn 'error' into an exit item with non-zero code so the model always gets a status (Grok Build already does this). bb side (plugins/provider-acp/src/event-translation.ts, translateAcpToolCallItem + completeAcpStartedToolItem): read rawOutput.exitCode when it is a finite number; when absent keep 1 for status 'failed' but OMIT exitCode for status 'completed' instead of fabricating 0; optionally mark completed execute calls with neither content nor rawOutput as failed. Promote issue-1529-repro.test.ts to permanent tests; no wire change so no HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump. Optional guidance in Cursor instructions: on 'returned no exit status', retry once with working_directory set to the workspace root.

1500.title: Forked threads have an empty timeline — fork should clone source events
1500.rootCauseOneLine: The fork path (thread-fork.ts → thread-create.ts resolveForkDescriptor → thread.start{fork:{sourceProviderThreadId}}) only clones the provider session and never copies/projects source events into the fork, so the timeline projection has nothing to render; additionally sourceSeqEnd is never mapped to the recorded turn/completed providerCheckpointId, so pi/claude-code/codex forks always clone the session tip regardless of the requested anchor.
1500.proposedFix: (A) Honor sourceSeqEnd at the provider: in thread-create.ts resolveForkDescriptor, resolve the root turn containing/preceding sourceSeqEnd and read its turn/completed.providerCheckpointId (reuse thread-edit-message.ts logic incl. codex turn-id case); add optional sourceProviderCheckpointId to threadStartCommandSchema.fork in host-daemon-contract (bump HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION); pass it through runtime.ts thread/fork (adapter already forwards it and rejects for tip-only providers); 400 for tip-only providers or missing checkpoint instead of silently forking the tip. (B) Make inherited history visible: copy source events with sequence <= sourceSeqEnd into the fork inside the fork transaction (rewrite threadId, mint ids, keep providerThreadId = source session, skip thread-start/provisioning bookkeeping, keep clientRequestId pairs intact), or alternatively persist sourceSeqEnd on the thread and lazily prepend the source window in the timeline builder. Repro test provided fails on main for both A and B.
1500.caveats: Priority/Effort project fields could not be read (token lacks read:project). Symptom 1 (empty timeline) is a long-standing design gap rather than a regression — docs/provider-bridge-protocol.md acknowledges it. The reporter's claim that directly inserted event rows are invisible until restart was refuted at the HTTP /timeline and CLI layer (timeline cache keys on maxSeq read from SQLite); the browser query cache not refetching is plausible but untested. Pi bridge writes session files to ~/.bb/pi-bridge-sessions even for the dev instance (read-only inspection only). Repro test uses expect.soft on assertion 1 so both failures show at once.

1363.title: Provider processes need one host-daemon lease owner tied to active turns
1363.rootCauseOneLine: No single lease owner: the daemon's idle reaper is Codex-only by default (providerSessionReaping experiment off), keys off daemon-internal turn state so a hung turn pins its process group forever (no max turn age), archive releases only archive-forwarding providers (Codex, not Claude Code), evictIdleEnvironments() has no caller, and the codex bridge exits before its SIGKILL escalation — so resident provider processes are bounded only by manual stop or daemon restart for everything except idle, healthy Codex sessions.
1363.proposedFix: (1) Make the agent runtime the lease owner: one record per provider session {threadId, providerThreadId, processKey, leaseKind turn|idle, leaseUntilMs}, refreshed on every provider event; release restorable sessions at the idle TTL for every provider by default (drop the Codex-only/experiment gate in findReapableIdleProviderSession/reapIdleProviderSessions), non-restorable at a longer TTL with a fresh-session notice. (2) Bound turns: per-thread "no provider event for N min" watchdog that fails the turn (provider_stalled) and stopThread-releases so server `stopping` settles and the process group is torn down. (3) Spawn provider children detached and kill the process group; in the codex bridge await SIGKILL escalation before process.exit in onClose/onSigterm. (4) On archive of an idle loaded thread whose provider lacks threadArchive forwarding, dispatch thread.stop {intent:"release"} (existing releaseIdleThreadRuntime). (5) Call RuntimeManager.evictIdleEnvironments() from the 5-minute maintenance pass. (6) Add a daemon local-API/CLI diagnostic listing pid -> provider -> processKey -> threadIds -> lease, and set BB_THREAD_ID on codex app-server children. Only (6) as a new host RPC would need a HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.
1363.caveats: Revision pass: rewrote env.sh/spawn.sh/procs.sh/rss-sum.sh to derive worktree, URLs, data dir, host id and project from `scripts/bb-dev-app status` and `bb machine list --json` (must be run with cwd inside the bb worktree or BB_WT set); re-ran them unmodified on a fresh third dev instance (:23519, host_hvuqh8u6ut) and reproduced exp. A/F again (codex bridge+app-server gone within 20 s of archive, claude CLI still resident 2 min later); both unit repro tests re-run with the same failures. Added inline full spawn commands, a glossary, header/claims-table wording fixes, and a Verification section. Not re-run in this pass: the 30-min reap ticks and the SIGSTOP / kill -9 experiments (B, E, G), which still rest on the author's log excerpts. Reporter's exact production numbers (17 app-servers / 7 code-mode hosts for 4 threads, OOM at 4 GiB, 124 sessions) remain unverifiable; the SIGSTOP hang is a stand-in; dev-mode tsx bridges inflate RSS vs production. Dev instance stopped with pnpm dev:stop; no worktree source changes left behind.

1334.title: Co-located execution workload can starve the bb server and leave threads spinning
1334.rootCauseOneLine: bb-app spawns server + primary host daemon (and every provider/agent descendant) as plain children in one cgroup, so cgroup-v2 memory.high reclaim throttling (mem_cgroup_handle_over_high) stalls the server along with the runaway workload; the only supported/documented deployment is that combined launcher (a split via the undocumented bb-server bin + `bb-app host-daemon join` works but is unadvertised, untested and heuristic for primary-host resolution), and since #421 host liveness ignores the heartbeat lease so a throttled daemon stays "connected" and threads stay "active" with no failure state or pressure signal.
1334.proposedFix: (1) Make the split deployment supported instead of accidental: expose the packaged bb-server bin as `bb-app server` in help/docs/CLI guide, have the installer optionally emit two systemd units (server with modest limits, daemon with the big MemoryHigh/MemoryMax, sharing the data dir so host-id-based primary-host resolution is deterministic), let `bb-app host-daemon` auto-enroll against a loopback server without the join dance, forward signals in the bb-server wrapper, and add a boot+enroll test; interim workaround today: bb-server.js in one unit + `bb-app --data-dir D host-daemon join --server-url http://127.0.0.1:P` in another. (2) On Linux, have the launcher place the daemon (and thus all provider/agent descendants) into its own child cgroup or systemd-run scope so the server keeps its own memory budget; fall back silently where unavailable. (3) Pressure-aware control plane: primary signals are the server's own event-loop stall monitor (flip a degraded flag shown in UI and gating new-turn admission, #1393) and daemon-reported raw cgroup memory.pressure/memory.events in heartbeats (bump HOST_DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION); secondary: "socket alive AND lease stale >> LEASE_TIMEOUT_MS" as an `unresponsive` host status in /api/v1/hosts, thread displayStatus and the UI. Plus mitigations: cap V8 heap from cgroup (#1748), reap idle provider processes sooner (#1604).
1334.caveats: Repro used systemd-run --scope with MemoryHigh=800M on a 58 GiB host rather than a real bb.service unit; the throttled hog only reached ~512 MiB so pressure was milder than the reporter's — the UI showed a ~30 s loading skeleton rather than an infinite spinner, while /health, /api/v1/threads and the daemon port did hit 5 s curl timeouts and the server was seen in D state in __mem_cgroup_handle_over_high (verifier reproduced independently; timeouts only appear several minutes after the hog starts, now documented in step 3). The full scope run was not re-executed in this revision; only the split-deployment cross-check (bb-server + host-daemon join, separate and shared data dirs) and the unit test were re-run in a fresh worktree at the base commit. Lease staleness is a weak detector for throttling (verifier's daemon never missed the lease; mine had one 35.7 s gap), so the unit test documents current behaviour rather than a reliable detector. Comment-2 claims (17 Codex app-servers, OOM kill at MemoryMax on 0.37.0) were checked against code but not reproduced. No provider turns were run. Port 48871 was occupied by another agent's leftover server, so the split check used 48881/48882.

1301.title: Thread timeline never unmounts history: 22k DOM nodes and 250-600ms long tasks after scrolling a large thread
1301.rootCauseOneLine: useThreadTimelineController prepends every fetched older page into one unbounded loadedTimeline.rows array and ThreadTimelineRows.TimelineRowsList renders all of them as real DOM (no windowing/virtualisation), so mounted DOM grows monotonically (2.4k -> 21k nodes on the 9,001-event seed thread) and each prepend is a 280-590 ms sync task (React mount of ~150 rows + forced layout via readOverflowMeasurement's useLayoutEffect on the growing document).

prReviews.topFinding: Not linked to the issue but is the fix candidate. With main merged it bounds the mobile DOM (21k -> ~1.7k nodes, long tasks 280-470ms -> 60-170ms on the same repro), but: (1) windowing toggles by swapping the per-row wrapper element type under the same key, so when a thread crosses 40 items or the viewport crosses 768px React remounts every row and drops all row-local state (hostile test ThreadTimelineRows.pr1384-threshold.test.tsx fails); (2) it only windows <768px, desktop still reaches 21k nodes / 589ms tasks; (3) branch is 151 commits behind main and conflicts with #1568's AutoHeightContainer snapRevision (needs rebase, and the windowed path drops AutoHeightContainer entirely).

1301.proposedFix: Window the top-level TimelineRowsList at all viewport widths: keep every row in flow with a stable-id-keyed wrapper that renders real content only near the viewport (IntersectionObserver with ~1 viewport margin) and otherwise a fixed-height placeholder using the last measured height; pin interacted rows and the active turn; never change wrapper component type when windowing is on/off (make it a passthrough instead) so no remount happens. Optionally cap loadedTimeline.rows to N pages around the viewport for memory, and cut per-page constant cost by batching conversation-message-overflow's synchronous layout read and skipping AutoHeightContainer's height animation for prepends. PR #1384's approach is the right shape once rebased and the threshold-remount and desktop-scope issues are fixed.
1301.caveats: Measurements are from a Vite dev build (React dev runtime) in headless Chromium on desktop hardware, so absolute ms are inflated vs production and iOS/WebKit momentum behaviour (the main focus of PR #1384's later commits) could not be verified. Fixture was seeded with 8 threads / 34,536 events (largest thread 9,001 events, same as the issue) rather than the 400k base plus jumbo append, so node/px counts differ slightly from the issue's (21,082 vs ~22k nodes; 68,302 vs 75,710 px). Server page sizes were 72-167 KB, not the ~10 KB the issue claims. PR #1384 was reviewed on a local merge with main (one conflict resolved by me by threading heightSnapRevision), not on the raw branch. I ran `dev-browser stop` at the end, which stops the shared dev-browser daemon (uptime showed it was long-lived); other agents' named browser pages may have been reset. Priority/Effort fields are not set on the issue.

1072.title: workspace-checkout-display (1.7MB) bundles Monaco/Eddie editor eagerly — should be lazy
1072.rootCauseOneLine: The HTML-shell preload of the 2.4MB shared chunk was fixed by #1071 (eager edge was App.tsx→usePluginFrontendBoot→plugin-frontend.ts, not the 85-line workspace-checkout-display module that merely lends the chunk its name); but the same 2.15MB chunk plus katex is still a static import of the lazy thread route (SplitWorkspaceRoute) via FilePreview→@pierre/diffs, markdown-preview→rehype-katex, PromptBoxInternal→tiptap, useThreadStorageBrowser→@pierre/trees and thread-operation-prompts→handlebars, so a thread page still parses ~3.3MB of editor/diff/tree/math/template code before first paint.

1690.title: Fail adding remote machine for new install
1690.rootCauseOneLine: AddMachineDialog collapses an unpaired/absent connect plugin to null and pairingCommand() silently falls back to the system-config serverUrl, which on a fresh desktop install is the loopback-bound http://127.0.0.1:38886, so it prints a curl installer no other machine can reach without telling the user to set up Remote access first.

prReviews.topFinding: Every 503 from the connect RPC is classified as transient 'unavailable'; a disabled connect plugin returns 503 'not running (status: disabled)', so the user gets 'Remote access isn't ready yet.' + a Try again dead end and the 'Waiting for the machine to connect…' spinner, with no link to enable the plugin (verified live and by unit probe). Core fix (loopback notice + Remote access link, tests, typecheck) is correct and passes the repro test.

1690.proposedFix: In AddMachineDialog: distinguish connect unpaired/absent/disabled from transient failure; when no connect machine code exists and the direct serverUrl hostname is loopback/unspecified, render an explanatory notice linking to /settings/plugins/connect and docs instead of a curl command, and hide the 'Waiting for the machine to connect…' box (PR #1695 does this; extend it to treat 503 'status: disabled' as unpaired). Optionally expose the server bind host in GET /system/config so reachability is server-owned rather than a client hostname heuristic.
1690.caveats: The reporter's second observation (Mac port bound to loopback only) is intentional behaviour since #1125, not a bug; the fix is guidance to bb connect/Tailscale Serve, not a LAN bind. Live repro was on a Linux dev instance (direct URL http://localhost:20022) rather than a packaged macOS desktop app; the desktop path yields http://127.0.0.1:38886 by construction (apps/desktop/src/types.ts) and the unit test uses that exact URL. Screenshots and PR test logs were partly produced by an earlier interrupted pass of this same task in this worktree; I re-verified the repro test failure on main and PR test/typecheck results in this session.
